pairs.question: Quid tu? servosne esse an liber mavelis, memora mihi.
pairs.answer: Proxumum quod sit bono quodque a malo longissume, id volo; quamquam non multum fuit molesta servitus, nec mihi secus erat quam si essem familiaris filius.
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks whether the prisoner would rather be slave or free; the disguised Philocrates answers. Answer runs from 'Proxumum' to the first full stop after 'familiaris filius'; nothing cut, it is a single contiguous reply. Dropped Tyndarus' intervening aside (lines 274-276) which is not part of the answer.

pairs.question: Quo de genere natust illic Philocrates?
pairs.answer: Polyplusio: quod genus illi est unum pollens atque honoratissumum.
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks of what family Philocrates was born; Philocrates (the disguised slave) answers. Answer is the complete reply through the full stop; the colon after 'Polyplusio' is internal, so the elaborating relative clause is kept as contiguous reply.

pairs.question: Quid ipsus hic? quo honore est illic?
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks in what honor the man himself is held there; the answer 'Summo, atque ab summis viris' directly answers the honor question. Full reply, nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quid divitiae, suntne opimae?
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks whether the riches are abundant; Philocrates answers metaphorically that the old man could render fat from them (= yes). Question taken from the unbracketed interrogative line 281; the preceding bracketed editorial line 280 ('[Tum igitur...]') is omitted as it is not needed for sense and is editorially deleted text.

pairs.question: Quid pater, vivitne?
pairs.answer: Vivom, cum inde abimus, liquimus; nunc vivatne necne, id Orcum scire oportet scilicet.
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks whether the father is alive; Philocrates answers that they left him alive on departure. Answer runs to the first full stop. Editorial supplement '<ne>' in 'vivat<ne>' had its brackets stripped, keeping 'vivatne'.

pairs.question: Quid erat ei nomen?
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks the father's name; Philocrates gives the (comic) name. Complete one-word answer, nothing cut.

pairs.question: Tenaxne pater est eius?
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks whether the father is stingy; Philocrates answers correcting to a stronger term ('nay, grasping'). Dropped the framing filler 'Quid tu ais?' that precedes the interrogative. Answer stops at 'pertinax' where the speaker turns to elaboration ('quin etiam ut magis noscas...', lines 290-292).

pairs.question: Vt sacrufices. Cui deorum?
pairs.answer: Mi hercle, nam ego nunc tibi sum summus Iuppiter.
pairs.derivation: Ergasilus tells Hegio to sacrifice ('Vt sacrufices'); Hegio asks 'Cui deorum?' (to which of the gods?). The setup 'Vt sacrufices' is kept verbatim so 'Cui' has its referent. Answer stops at the first full stop after 'Iuppiter'; the following self-aggrandizing list (line 864) is elaboration and is cut.

pairs.question: Quid tu per barbaricas urbes iuras?
pairs.answer: Quia enim item asperae sunt ut tuom victum autumabas esse.
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks why Ergasilus swears by barbarian cities; Ergasilus answers that they are as rough as Hegio claimed his food to be. Complete reply, nothing cut.

pairs.question: Sed Stalagmus quoius erat tunc nationis, cum hinc abit?
pairs.derivation: Ergasilus asks of what nationality Stalagmus was when he left; Hegio answers 'Siculus.' One-word direct answer; Ergasilus' following joke (line 888) is a new turn, not part of the answer.

pairs.question: Dic, bonan fide tu mi istaec verba dixisti?
pairs.derivation: Hegio asks whether Ergasilus told him these things in good faith; Ergasilus answers 'Bona' (in good [faith]). Complete one-word answer.

pairs.question: Et eum vendidi. Cui homini?
pairs.answer: Theodoromedi in Alide Polyplusio, sex minis.
pairs.derivation: Stalagmus confesses he sold the boy ('et eum vendidi'); Hegio asks 'Cui homini?' (to what man?). The setup 'Et eum vendidi' is kept verbatim from Stalagmus' immediately preceding line so 'eum' has its referent. Answer gives buyer and price; complete reply through the full stop after 'sex minis'.

pairs.question: Quam diu id factum est?
pairs.derivation: Philocrates asks how long ago the sale took place (Hegio having just reported, lines 978-979, that Stalagmus claims to have sold his son); Stalagmus answers 'this makes the twentieth year.' Complete reply.

pairs.question: Quid erat ei nomen? si vera dicis, memoradum mihi.
pairs.answer: Paegnium vocitatust, post vos indidistis Tyndaro.
pairs.derivation: Philocrates asks the boy's name; Stalagmus answers that he was called Paegnium, later renamed Tyndarus. Complete reply through the full stop.

pairs.question: Cur ego te non novi?
pairs.answer: Quia mos est oblivisci hominibus neque novisse cuius nihili sit faciunda gratia.
pairs.derivation: Philocrates asks why he does not recognize Stalagmus; Stalagmus answers that men forget those whose goodwill counts for nothing. Complete reply, contiguous across lines 985-986.

pairs.question: Dic mihi, isne istic fuit, quem vendidisti meo patri, qui mihi peculiaris datus est?
pairs.derivation: Philocrates asks whether the one Stalagmus sold to his father, given to him as his own slave, was that person; Stalagmus answers 'Huius filius' (this man's son), identifying him. Terse but genuinely answers the identifying question.
